subject: Post-demo: geo latency gates, failover plan & data residency constraints
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@nimbushealth.com>; Sara Liu <sara.liu@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: geo latency gates, failover plan & data residency constraints

Hi Alex / Sara —

Appreciate you both taking the time today. Quick recap and a concrete set of asks so we can lock the performance and residency constraints into the SOW. Below are the items we discussed (keeps to the quantitative gates we need to validate during your pilot).

1) Latency gates (observed p95 generation time for short prompts, 256 tokens max):
   - US (us-east): <= 220 ms p95
   - EU (eu-west): <= 320 ms p95
   - APAC (ap-southeast): <= 450 ms p95

2) Throughput & concurrency:
   - Sustained concurrency target: 120 concurrent requests per region (steady), burst to 400 for 10s windows
   - Token throughput expected: ~1.8M tokens/minute across the account during peak for your notifications pipeline

3) Streaming / first-byte SLAs:
   - First-byte for streaming responses <= 60 ms after request acceptance for US/EU; <= 100 ms APAC
   - Per-token tail latency target (p99) <= 95 ms

4) Data residency constraints:
   - Patient-derived PII payloads must remain in EU for EU-origin traffic (logs masked, encrypted, KMS in customer EU account).
   - Audit logs (redacted) can be pushed to your central S3 in us-east only after anonymization (per procurement ask).

Next steps and asks from Nimbus:
- Confirm which endpoints are EU-only vs global (we need a list of routes and expected region of origin).
- Share a 48-hour peak sample (timestamps + approximate request sizes) so we can size reserved pools.
- Procurement: confirm whether the KMS will be customer-managed in EU or you want Redwood to provision (we can support either).

Attached: redwood_geo_perf_matrix_v1.xlsx (high-level perf estimates + recommended config per region). Demo recording attached.

I’ll loop in engineering (Rishi / Dylan) below for the sizing questions; happy to hop on a short follow-up to finalize the pilot acceptance criteria.

Thanks,
Mina
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@nimbushealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Liu <sara.liu@nimbushealth.com>; Procurement <procurement@nim-health.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: geo latency gates, failover plan & data residency constraints

Thanks Mina — this is helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side before we finalize the pilot SOW:

- EU-only routes: patient intake UI and document redaction service. Both are EU-originated traffic and must remain in EU for inference and unredacted logs.
- Global routes: choice-engine and generic content generation can be routed to US for cost reasons.
- On KMS: Procurement prefers a customer-managed KMS in EU. Can you confirm Redwood’s recommended approach for cross-region key usage if we keep KMS in eu-west only?
- On concurrency: the 120 steady number is per-region right? Our ops team will extract the 48-hour peak sample and send later today.

Also, one ask from engineering: can Redwood demonstrate a failover model that preserves EU residency by using EU spare capacity first, then, if saturated, route to an EU-certified partner in APAC for EU customers (if permitted)?

Alex
Lead Product Manager, Nimbus Health
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@nimbushealth.com>; Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 16:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: geo latency gates, failover plan & data residency constraints

Alex — quick technical responses inline to help procurement and engineering: 

- KMS and cross-region keys: you can keep keys in eu-west. Redwood supports envelope encryption where per-region data plane uses a locally-wrapped data key and the master key stays in your EU KMS. For cross-region push of anonymized audit logs to us-east, we recommend re-wrapping with a US key only after a deterministic anonymization step we can jointly validate. (We’ll include the anonymization script in the pilot repo).

- EU-preserving failover: we cannot route EU-origin raw data to non-EU regions unless you explicitly allow it. For the scenario you described, we can configure a policy: primary EU -> secondary EU certified partner pool (contracted) -> tertiary APAC partner but only after an explicit patient-consent flag or if payload is pre-redacted. That preserves compliance posture while giving you burst protection.

- Concurrency sizing: based on your expected token sizes and the 48-hour sample you’ll send, our recommendation will be to reserve 2x of observed 95th percentile concurrency per region to allow headroom for burst autoscaling. We’ll include continuous KV caching to cut repeated prefix costs.

Action items from Redwood (we own):
- (R1) Validate 48-hour sample and produce a region-by-region reserved pool proposal (ETA 48 hours after sample).
- (R2) Share anonymization script and sample audit pipeline for procurement review (ETA 24 hours).
- (R3) Provide a pilot acceptance checklist with measurement harness for p95/p99 across regions (ETA 72 hours).

Attachment: redwood_geo_perf_matrix_v1.xlsx (updated with notes). I’ll also put the anonymization script in the Drive link Mina shared.

— Rishi
Senior Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@nimbushealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>; Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Jones <alex.jones@nimbushealth.com>; Procurement <procurement@nim-health.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: geo latency gates, failover plan & data residency constraints

Thanks — that addresses the major concerns. Procurement: we want customer-managed KMS in EU and the anonymization step before logs leave EU. Ops will push the 48-hour sample by EOD.

Accept the proposed action items (R1,R2,R3). Can we schedule a 30-minute sync Thursday to review the reserved pool proposal? If so, please send a calendar invite.

Sara
Engineering Manager, Nimbus Health
